DENVER, Colorado — Latino voters in Colorado's 8th Congressional District are broadly pessimistic about the country's direction and increasingly critical of President Trump's job performance, according to new polling from the 2026 Latino Policy Agenda Survey.

The results show increased criticism toward Trump as well as Republican Congressman Gabe Evans, who was endorsed by the president and leaned heavily on that support during his election bid in 2024.

The most recent polling data from The Economist and YouGov, taken August 21-28 found that 36 percent of Hispanic voters approved of how Trump is handling his job.

It is a 13-point increase from May 22-26, when 23 percent approved of the president’s job performance, according to polling. It is a further 5-point increase from polling data recorded July 25-27, when 31 percent of Hispanic voters approved of the president. The number was slightly higher, 34 percent, in poll data taken June 26-29. [...] The president’s popularity differs across the country.

results.content: Civiqs, a nonpartisan online polling firm that surveys presidential approval on a rolling basis, puts Trump’s current approval in Idaho at 49 percent, with 41 percent disapproving as of Thursday. That figure has fluctuated near that line in recent weeks. The Idaho Democratic Party cited the same Civiqs data in a statement released Aug. 19. [...] Among racial groups, white Idahoans, who make up the large majority of the state’s population, approve at 51 percent and disapprove at 40 percent. Black Idahoans approve at 33 percent and disapprove at 67 percent. Hispanic and Latino residents approve at 45 percent and disapprove at 51 percent.
